title: Complete, stably ordered SDDC Manager credential inventory
prompt:
Implement the exported Get-VcfSddcManagerCredentialInventory function in src/VcfSddcManager.CredentialInventory.psm1. The runner installs the genuine VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager PowerCLI module version 13.5.0.25380678 as an environment prerequisite; page the collection with its Invoke-VcfGetCredentials cmdlet against the connected server rather than with a direct HTTP client.

getCredentials (GET /v1/credentials) is a page-number paginated collection whose first page is 0. Return the collection in full: keep requesting successive pages until every page counted by pageMetadata.totalPages has been read, and issue no request past the last page. Note that pageMetadata.pageSize reports how many elements the page just returned actually contains rather than the page size that was requested, and that a totalPages of 0 means the first request already covered an empty collection. Send pageNumber and pageSize explicitly on every request.

Emit the accumulated credentials in a single stable total order that does not depend on where the page boundaries fall or on the order the server happens to return elements within a page: ascending ordinal comparison by resource.resourceName, then credentialType, then username, then id. Return the SDK's own Credential model objects.

ResourceName, ResourceType, DomainName and AccountType are optional filters. Forward each one only when the caller actually supplied it; an unset filter must be absent from the query string rather than sent as an empty resourceName=, resourceType=, domainName= or accountType=. Never send the deprecated resourceIp parameter. The public parameter contract already present in the stub must remain compatible.

Use docs/contract.json as the local REST contract; its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Run python3 -B tests/verify.py. Only src/VcfSddcManager.CredentialInventory.psm1 is an implementation file; the module manifest, docs/ and tests/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed. The verifier drives the genuine SDK against a contract-pinned loopback SDDC Manager mock and never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
